why: The student explains the difference correctly: an array element can be read because `new` gives it a default value of 0, while a plain local variable has no value until it is assigned. This links the two rules, as the definite_assignment–array_default_values parallel edge describes.

concepts.why: The answer has no separate claim about variables in general.
Says correctly that creating the array with new is what puts the default 0 in every slot.
Declaration syntax and scope are not discussed.
Says nothing about primitive types themselves.
Says nothing about the array declaration.
Mentions giving a value only as part of the definite-assignment contrast.

concepts.quote: a local variable has no value until you give it one
concepts.why: Contrasts an unassigned local variable with array elements that get default values, which is the parallel relation.

concepts.quote: new fills the array with 0s, but a local variable has no value until you give it one
concepts.why: Explains that a[0] can be read because new gives it a default, unlike a local variable, which answers the question correctly.
